- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk aversion.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes; apply a 1–3 day lag correction: if price spiked 3+ days ago, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 2σ above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 1–3% to align with historical volatility.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 2-day smoothing buffer before updating forecast.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1% to initial forecast to account for lagged momentum.
